# image-drop-upload

> An embeddable image drop zone: a dependency-free browser widget with previews, and a
> framework-free Node upload handler. The widget shows each picked file as a thumbnail
> with its size and a remove button, identifies files by their leading bytes rather than
> their extension, and either rides along with an ordinary form or uploads on its own with
> progress and cancellation. Published on npm as `image-drop-upload` (v3, MIT, Node >= 20).

**The two halves are independent.** `image-drop-upload` is a plain JS class that mounts
into any DOM element — no framework, no jQuery, no icon font, zero runtime dependencies,
16 KB JS + 2 KB CSS gzipped. `image-drop-upload/server` is a single `(req, res)` function
that mounts in Express, AdonisJS, Fastify, Nest or bare `node:http`; its only dependency is
busboy, declared as an optional peer so pages using the widget against a PHP/Python/Go
backend never install it. Either half works without the other.

**Install**

```bash
npm install image-drop-upload      # the widget
npm install busboy                 # only if you also use the Node handler
```

**As a plain form field — no server changes at all.** Leave `endpoint` unset and the files
ride along with the form; the existing backend sees an ordinary `multipart/form-data` post.

```js
import { DropPreview } from 'image-drop-upload';
import 'image-drop-upload/style.css';

new DropPreview('#images', { name: 'images[]' });
```

**Uploading on its own**

```js
const drop = new DropPreview('#images', { endpoint: '/api/upload', autoUpload: true });
drop.on('uploaded', ({ answer }) => console.log(answer.uploaded));
```

```js
import express from 'express';
import { createUploadHandler } from 'image-drop-upload/server';

const app = express();
app.use('/api/upload', createUploadHandler({ root: './uploads' }));
app.listen(3000);
```

**Against a backend of your own.** Point `endpoint` at any URL that accepts a `POST` of
`multipart/form-data` with files under the field `images[]` (renameable via `name`). Any
2xx marks the request's files sent; a non-2xx may carry
`{ "code": "TOO_LARGE", "error": "…" }` for the whole request, or
`{ "failures": [{ "name": "a.png", "code": "TOO_LARGE", "error": "…" }] }` to mark single
files and keep the rest. `filesPerRequest` is 1 by default, so a dropped connection resumes
at the file it stopped on.

**Widget options** (`new DropPreview(target, options)`; `target` is an element or selector)

```js
{
  endpoint: null,         // POST here; null keeps it a plain form field
  name: 'images[]',       // form field name
  fields: null,           // extra form fields sent with an upload
  headers: null,          // object or function — for authorisation tokens
  credentials: 'same-origin',

  accept: [],             // MIME types; empty means every image format known
  allowSvg: false,        // SVG is XML that can carry script; opt-in
  limits: null,           // { maxFileSize, maxFiles, maxTotalSize, maxPixels }
  compress: null,         // shrink pictures in the browser before sending
  retry: null,            // send a failed upload again
  filesPerRequest: 1,     // files in one request; 0 sends the whole queue at once

  autoUpload: false,
  showUploadButton: true,
  showClearButton: true,

  reorder: true,          // drag a tile, or Alt+arrow on a focused one
  paste: true,            // Ctrl+V; 'document' listens on the whole page
  camera: 'auto',         // a "Take a photo" button where the pointer is coarse
  capture: 'environment',

  locale: null,           // 'en' | 'uk' | 'es' | 'de' | 'fr' | your dictionary
  theme: null,            // colours, fonts, metrics
  colorScheme: 'auto',    // 'auto' | 'light' | 'dark'
}
```

`limits` defaults: `maxFileSize` 10 MB, `maxFiles` 20, `maxTotalSize` 100 MB, `maxPixels`
50 M. `maxPixels` guards against decompression bombs: a 30 KB PNG declaring 40000x40000
costs gigabytes to decode, so the check runs when the preview is built.

**Methods, properties and events**

```js
await drop.add(fileList);   drop.remove(id);   drop.clear();
await drop.upload();        drop.cancel();     drop.destroy();
drop.files;                 drop.totalBytes;   drop.busy;
drop.describeError(code, detail);              // code -> text in the active language

drop.on('change',   ({ files }) => {});
drop.on('rejected', ({ rejected }) => {});     // [{ file, code, detail }]
drop.on('uploaded', ({ answer, files }) => {});
drop.on('error',    ({ error, code, message }) => {});
```

`on()` returns a function that unsubscribes. Refusals carry a `code`, never a sentence, so
code can branch on them.

**Handler options** (`createUploadHandler(options)` from `image-drop-upload/server`)

```js
{
  root: './uploads',         // required; the one directory files may land in
  basePath: '',              // prefix to strip when the host does not rewrite req.url
  field: 'images[]',
  accept: [],  allowSvg: false,
  onConflict: 'rename',      // 'rename' | 'refuse' | 'overwrite'
  rename: null,              // (name, { type }) => string
  limits: {
    maxFileSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
    maxFiles: 20,                      // per request; see perClient for per-person
    maxRequestSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,
    maxPixels: 50 * 1024 * 1024,
    maxBytesPerSecond: 0,              // server-side rate limit; 0 is no limit
    perClient: null,                   // quota across requests
    minFreeSpace: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
  },
  maxConcurrent: 8,          // uploads in flight; beyond that, 503
  allowedOrigins: undefined, // same-origin only by default; false disables the check
  authorize: (req, ctx) => true,
  onWarning: (message, detail) => {},
  sessions: null,            // { identify(req), scope, … } — a folder per visitor
  scan: null,                // { service: 'virustotal', apiKey } or your own check()
  storage: null,             // createS3Storage({ bucket, region, … }); local disk otherwise
}
```

The answer is `{ uploaded: [{ name, original, size, type }], failures: [{ name, code,
error, params }], fields: {} }` — one bad file does not fail the batch. `UploadService`
from the same entry point does the filesystem work alone, for a framework that parses
multipart itself.

**Error codes.** Client and server share a vocabulary: `NOT_AN_IMAGE`, `SVG_REFUSED`,
`TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `TOO_LARGE`, `TOTAL_TOO_LARGE`, `TOO_MANY`, `EMPTY`, `DUPLICATE`,
`QUOTA`, `BUSY`, `DENIED`, `ABORTED`, `NETWORK`, `HTTP_ERROR`, `CROSS_ORIGIN`,
`NOT_MULTIPART`, `NO_FILES`, `INVALID_BODY`, `NO_SESSION`, `INVALID_SESSION`, `INTERNAL`.

**Optional feature blocks.** Each is one option; leave it out and that code never runs.
*Compression* (`compress: { maxWidth, maxHeight, fit, quality, format, stripMetadata,
skipIfLarger }`) resizes and re-encodes on the page via canvas — `quality: 'auto'` is 0.85,
`'lossless'` strips metadata only, and a picture already inside the box is left alone.
*Retry* (`retry: { attempts: 3, delay: 1000, backoff: 2, maxDelay: 30000 }`) repeats
connection failures, never refusals, with Cancel cutting the wait short. *Sessions*
(`sessions: { identify(req) }`) gives each visitor a subdirectory and reports an `owner`.
*Malware screening* (`scan`) sends a SHA-256 to VirusTotal or your own scanner — the file
never leaves the server; `onUnknown` defaults to `accept`, `onError` to `reject`.
*S3* (`createS3Storage`) signs requests with SigV4 from `node:crypto`, no SDK.

**Security posture.** Type is sniffed from leading bytes on both sides, the client's check
only to give the user a reason. Unsafe names are refused rather than repaired (traversal in
any spelling, NUL bytes, Windows device names, trailing dots). Uploads land under a
temporary name and are renamed only when whole; a dead request is cleaned up. Cross-origin
`multipart/form-data` posts are rejected by default, since they are not preflighted.

**Languages and themes.** English (default), Ukrainian, Spanish, German, French, or your
own dictionary object; plurals follow each language's rule and sizes are localised. Light
and dark themes follow the system or can be forced; every colour, font and metric is a CSS
variable settable through `theme`.

**Limitations.** Images only (ten formats identified). Previews are `background-image`, so
animation plays as the browser sees fit. Compression re-encodes via canvas — no lossless
JPEG recompression. Dimensions are read from the header, not measured. The queue is held in
a hidden input through `DataTransfer`, which has no fallback. HEIC/AVIF upload but show an
empty tile where the browser cannot decode them. No chunking inside a single file. Needs a
2023-or-newer browser (container queries, `:has()`) and Node 20+.

## API reference

- [types/index.d.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/types/index.d.ts): the widget's full typed surface — options, events, exported helpers
- [types/server.d.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/types/server.d.ts): handler options, `UploadService`, storage backends, quotas, scanning
- [src/index.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/src/index.js): every client export, annotated
- [server/index.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/server/index.js): every server export, annotated
- [package.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/package.json): entry points, exports map, peer dependencies

## Examples

- [demo/main.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/demo/main.js): a working page exercising language, theme, compression and resize controls
- [demo/index.html](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/demo/index.html): the markup it mounts into
- [server/standalone.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insider515/drag-and-drop-preview-images-module/master/server/standalone.js): the demo server, and a minimal `node:http` mount

- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/image-drop-upload): published releases
